newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-FALKIRK'S LATE EQUALISER KEEPS PRESSURE ON BURNS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-FALKIRK'S LATE EQUALISER KEEPS PRESSURE ON BURNS.

text.p: Celtic's bid to ease the pain of conceding the title to Rangers by winning the Scottish Cup received an unexpected setback when they were held to a 1-1 draw by first division Falkirk in their semifinal at Ibrox on Saturday.

Falkirk's towering 2.01 metres tall central defender Kevin James scored a magnificent 82nd-minute equaliser to cancel out Tommy Johnson's first goal for Celtic since his recent 2.4 million pounds ($3.9 million) signing from Aston Villa and set up a replay on the same ground on April 23.
That match now becomes crucial for Celtic manager Tommy Burns whose position at the club appears to be under threat -- with Kevin Keegan being touted as a possible successor.

Certainly his much-vaunted foreign strike force of Italian Paolo di Canio, German Andreas Thom and Portugal's Jorge Cadete will have to do more than they did in front of 45,261 on Saturday if Celtic are to reach the final for the 47th time.
They looked incapable of finding a way through until Johnson pounced in the 66th minute to score from close range after Falkirk keeper Craig Nelson's series of saves kept his side in the tie.
Falkirk, who have been in two Cup finals -- 1913 and 1957 -- and won both, were never overawed by Celtic and their 10,000 fans went wild with delight after James's late equaliser.
Celtic had a let-off as early as the 10th minute when Falkirk had a goal disallowed after Scott Crabbe pounced on a ball which came back off a post but there was little doubt the effort was offside.
The other semifinal between Kilmarnock and Dundee United will be played on Monday night at Easter Road, Edinburgh.
In the league, Motherwell pushed bottom club Raith closer to relegation with a 5-0 home victory while Dunfermline drew 1-1 with Hibernian and Hearts drew 0-0 with Aberdeen.
